{{quote|I greet you eagerly, </em>Mia'cova<em>.|[[Moghedien]]{{ref/book|7|25}}}}
'''''Mia'cova''''' is a phrase in the [[Old Tongue]] meaning "one who owns me," or simply "my owner." The title is actually "lashed together," as [[Moghedien]] thought, from "''mia''" meaning "my" and "''cova''" meaning "owner" or "one who owns."

While in a [[vacuole]], [[Shaidar Haran]] conditioned Moghedien with punishment to refer to him with the title. After being freed from the vacuole, Moghedien also used the title for [[Moridin]], as he was current holder of her [[mindtrap|''cour'souvra'']].
